clinicalPearls: Fatigable ptosis relieved by rest or ice suggests myasthenia gravis
Pralidoxime must precede enzyme ageing in organophosphate poisoning
Physostigmine crosses into brain; neostigmine does not
Cholinergic crisis adds salivation, miosis and fasciculations to weakness
reference.pathophysiology: Autoimmune receptor loss reduces endplate potentials below threshold during repeated firing, producing fatigable weakness that cholinesterase inhibition temporarily overcomes by prolonging transmitter action. Organophosphates instead phosphorylate cholinesterases globally, so muscarinic, nicotinic and central toxicity proceed together until atropine blockade and enzyme reactivation or resynthesis.
